name: stroke (Elf-stroke, fairy stroke)
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

attributes.attribute: a sudden paralysis blamed on the fairies
believed to be a blow from the fairies
left in the place of a person taken away
provoked by cutting a fairy tree or breaking a fairy mound

text: Stroke is the old name of a sudden fall once blamed on the good people. It is also called an elf-stroke or a fairy stroke. Today a stroke is known to be a paralysis, brought on when the flow of blood to the brain is cut or a clot forms there. The older people had no such knowledge. They read the sudden fall as a blow struck by the fairies, who were angered and used their power on the offender. Those who slipped into a deep sleep were said to have been taken away by the fairies and a changeling left in their place. The stroke could be provoked by wrong against the good people. Cutting down a fairy tree, plowing through a fairy mound, or touching any ground the fairies used could invite the blow. This belief kept many old holy sites safe for long ages.
